teaser: Why a small security firm's grand website reaches the readers who won't buy and loses the ones who need it, and what to sell instead.
core_idea: A one-to-five person security firm with a grand website selling a SOC, XDR, red teaming and audits faces a tragic symmetry: the security experts who understand it buy from established providers, while the small businesses who need it cannot read it, since only 9% of UK micro businesses knew of Cyber Essentials in 2025. Selling at the right altitude means naming the people, the place and the price, and selling outcomes an owner understands: open after ransomware, nobody logging in as you, laptops looked after, client data handled, AI tools doing what you meant. Every service must pass three questions: sold it, can deliver it, readable by the buyer who needs it.
